vertebral.name: Vertebral artery
vertebral.text: Ascends through the transverse foramina from C6 to C1 (only the vertebral vein passes through C7's); grooves the upper surface of the atlas

subclavian.name: Subclavian artery
subclavian.from: Brachiocephalic trunk on the right, the aortic arch on the left
subclavian.text: Becomes the axillary artery at the lateral border of the 1st rib. Two branches join the anastomosis around the scapula

suprascapular.name: Suprascapular artery
suprascapular.text: Back of the shoulder. Runs with the suprascapular nerve, above the superior transverse scapular ligament

axillary.name: Axillary artery
axillary.from: Subclavian artery, at the lateral border of the 1st rib
axillary.text: Ends at the lower border of teres major. Three parts, set by pectoralis minor in front of it (1st above it, 2nd behind it, 3rd below it); the plexus cords are named for where they sit around it

thoracoacromial.name: Thoracoacromial artery
thoracoacromial.text: Acromial, clavicular, deltoid and pectoral branches; joins the anastomosis around the glenohumeral joint

subscapular.name: Subscapular artery
subscapular.text: A short trunk that splits into the thoracodorsal and circumflex scapular arteries

thoracodorsal.name: Thoracodorsal artery
thoracodorsal.text: Superficial back (latissimus dorsi); runs with the thoracodorsal nerve

circumflex_scapular.name: Circumflex scapular artery
circumflex_scapular.text: Curves round the lateral border of the scapula, deep to teres minor and infraspinatus, into the scapular anastomosis

ant_circumflex_humeral.name: Anterior circumflex humeral artery
ant_circumflex_humeral.text: Encircles the surgical neck of the humerus laterally; a branch to the glenohumeral joint

post_circumflex_humeral.name: Posterior circumflex humeral artery
post_circumflex_humeral.text: Encircles the surgical neck medially and joins the anterior one; runs with the axillary nerve
post_circumflex_humeral.clinical: A surgical neck fracture threatens it with the axillary nerve

brachial.name: Brachial artery
brachial.from: Axillary artery, at the lower border of teres major
brachial.text: Runs medial to biceps, in front of coracobrachialis and brachialis; ends in the cubital fossa as the radial (lateral) and ulnar (medial) arteries. In the cubital fossa: biceps Tendon, brachial Artery, median Nerve (TAN, lateral to medial)
brachial.clinical: Blood pressure is taken over it. It lies against the medial humeral shaft, so a mid-shaft or supracondylar fracture can injure it

deep_brachial.name: Profunda brachii (deep brachial) artery
deep_brachial.text: Posterior compartment of the arm, in the radial groove with the radial nerve; becomes the radial collateral artery at the elbow
deep_brachial.clinical: Adherent to the humerus in the radial groove, so a mid-shaft fracture threatens it with the radial nerve

sup_ulnar_collateral.name: Superior ulnar collateral artery
sup_ulnar_collateral.text: The network around the elbow; joins the posterior ulnar recurrent

inf_ulnar_collateral.name: Inferior ulnar collateral artery
inf_ulnar_collateral.text: The network around the elbow; joins the anterior ulnar recurrent

radial.name: Radial artery
radial.from: Brachial artery, in the cubital fossa
radial.text: Lateral forearm, deep to brachioradialis; at the wrist it wraps laterally onto the back, across the floor of the anatomical snuffbox, and enters the palm between the two heads of the 1st dorsal interosseous to form the deep palmar arch
radial.clinical: Radial pulse between the flexor carpi radialis and abductor pollicis longus tendons, and in the snuffbox. A scaphoid fragment cut off from its radial artery supply can undergo avascular necrosis

radial_recurrent.name: Recurrent radial artery
radial_recurrent.text: Joins the radial collateral artery in the network around the elbow

ulnar.name: Ulnar artery
ulnar.from: Brachial artery, in the cubital fossa
ulnar.text: Medial forearm, deep to pronator teres; enters the wrist beside the pisiform, over the flexor retinaculum, through Guyon's canal with the ulnar nerve, and forms the superficial palmar arch
ulnar.clinical: Not in the carpal tunnel: it passes on top of the flexor retinaculum

ant_ulnar_recurrent.name: Anterior ulnar recurrent artery
ant_ulnar_recurrent.text: Joins the inferior ulnar collateral artery around the elbow

post_ulnar_recurrent.name: Posterior ulnar recurrent artery
post_ulnar_recurrent.text: Joins the superior ulnar collateral artery around the elbow

common_interosseous.name: Common interosseous artery
common_interosseous.from: Ulnar artery, at the distal cubital fossa
common_interosseous.text: Splits almost at once into the anterior and posterior interosseous arteries

ant_interosseous.name: Anterior interosseous artery
ant_interosseous.text: Runs with the anterior interosseous nerve on the front of the interosseous membrane

post_interosseous.name: Posterior interosseous artery
post_interosseous.text: Passes into the posterior compartment above the interosseous membrane

sup_palmar_arch.name: Superficial palmar arch
sup_palmar_arch.from: Mainly the ulnar artery, completed by the superficial palmar branch of the radial
sup_palmar_arch.text: Just deep to the palmar aponeurosis; gives the common palmar digital arteries, which divide into proper palmar digital arteries

deep_palmar_arch.name: Deep palmar arch
deep_palmar_arch.from: Mainly the radial artery, completed by the deep branch of the ulnar
deep_palmar_arch.text: Across the metacarpals just past their bases; gives 3 palmar metacarpal arteries

radialis_indicis.name: Radialis indicis artery
radialis_indicis.text: The lateral side of the index finger

palmar_digital.name: Common and proper palmar digital arteries
palmar_digital.text: Common palmar digital arteries divide into proper palmar digital arteries along the fingers

internal_iliac.name: Internal iliac artery
internal_iliac.text: Gives the superior and inferior gluteal, internal pudendal and obturator arteries

sup_gluteal.name: Superior gluteal artery
sup_gluteal.from: Internal iliac artery (its largest and final branch)
sup_gluteal.text: Gluteal region: leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen above piriformis, with the superior gluteal nerve and vein

inf_gluteal.name: Inferior gluteal artery
inf_gluteal.text: Gluteal region: leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen below piriformis, with the inferior gluteal nerve and vein; supplies the posterior thigh too
inf_gluteal.clinical: Part of the cruciate anastomosis round the hip with the medial and lateral circumflex and 1st perforating arteries

internal_pudendal.name: Internal pudendal artery
internal_pudendal.text: Out the greater sciatic foramen below piriformis, then into the perineum through the lesser; supplies the perineum. The pudendal nerve (S2-S4) runs with it

obturator.name: Obturator artery
obturator.text: Medial compartment of the thigh, with the perforating branches

external_iliac.name: External iliac artery
external_iliac.text: Becomes the femoral artery under the inguinal ligament

femoral.name: Femoral artery
femoral.from: External iliac artery, under the inguinal ligament
femoral.text: Anterior thigh. In the femoral triangle (NAVEL, lateral to medial: nerve, artery, vein, empty canal, lymphatics), inside the femoral sheath; becomes the popliteal artery after the adductor hiatus
femoral.clinical: Superficial in the femoral triangle, so easily injured; the femoral pulse

deep_femoral.name: Deep femoral (profunda femoris) artery
deep_femoral.text: Its perforating branches (usually 3-4) pierce adductor magnus to the posterior thigh and supply all three compartments; gives the medial and lateral circumflex femoral arteries

perforating.name: Perforating arteries
perforating.text: Pierce adductor magnus to the posterior thigh; supply the medial and posterior compartments (the posterior compartment has no artery of its own)

med_circumflex_femoral.name: Medial circumflex femoral artery
med_circumflex_femoral.text: Most of the femoral head and neck
med_circumflex_femoral.clinical: Cruciate anastomosis (medial and lateral circumflex, inferior gluteal, 1st perforating) keeps the leg alive after femoral artery ligation

lat_circumflex_femoral.name: Lateral circumflex femoral artery
lat_circumflex_femoral.text: Lateral thigh: an ascending branch to the femoral neck, a transverse one round the femur and a descending one to the knee (the knee's collateral circulation)

popliteal.name: Popliteal artery
popliteal.from: Femoral artery, after the adductor hiatus
popliteal.text: Through the popliteal fossa, deepest of artery, vein, nerve (AVN); splits at its lower border into the anterior and posterior tibial arteries
popliteal.clinical: Popliteal aneurysm is the most common peripheral aneurysm: embolism, thrombosis, rupture; 80% have no symptoms

ant_tibial.name: Anterior tibial artery
ant_tibial.text: Through a gap at the top of the interosseous membrane into the anterior compartment with the deep fibular nerve, between tibialis anterior and extensor digitorum longus; becomes dorsalis pedis between the malleoli

post_tibial.name: Posterior tibial artery
post_tibial.text: Deep posterior compartment with the tibial nerve, between flexor digitorum longus and tibialis posterior; behind the medial malleolus through the tarsal tunnel (Tom, Dick, And Not Harry) into the medial and lateral plantar arteries
post_tibial.clinical: Pulse between the medial malleolus and the Achilles tendon; invert the foot to relax the flexor retinaculum

fibular.name: Fibular artery
fibular.from: Posterior tibial artery, its largest branch
fibular.text: Down toward the fibula within flexor hallucis longus; muscular branches to the posterior and lateral compartments

dorsalis_pedis.name: Dorsalis pedis artery
dorsalis_pedis.from: Anterior tibial artery, past the malleoli
dorsalis_pedis.text: Dorsum of the foot, with the deep fibular nerve: lateral tarsal and arcuate branches; the deep plantar artery dives between metatarsals 1 and 2 to the sole
dorsalis_pedis.clinical: Pulse lateral to the extensor hallucis longus tendon; diminished or absent = peripheral arterial disease

deep_plantar.name: Deep plantar artery
deep_plantar.text: Dives between the 1st and 2nd metatarsals to complete the deep plantar arch

lat_plantar.name: Lateral plantar artery
lat_plantar.text: Runs along the lateral sole, then arches medially as the deep plantar arch

med_plantar.name: Medial plantar artery
med_plantar.text: Medial sole and big toe; contributes to the deep plantar arch

plantar_arch.name: Deep plantar arch
plantar_arch.from: Lateral plantar artery, completed by the deep plantar artery
plantar_arch.text: Gives four plantar metatarsal arteries, which go on as the digital arteries
